# A prop fyne has no setter for fails the build.
#
# A prop *is* its write by the time it reaches a platform: passReactivity and
# passDeclarative turn `text(value=greeting)` into `__n0.value = greeting`, and
# fyne's OnPropAssign is where that becomes `SetText`. A prop the widget's Spec
# names no setter for therefore does not render a stale value -- it does not
# render at all, and returning no statements said so to nobody.
#
# gtk4 has reported its own unsettable props all along. This is fyne given the
# same, and the whole of what makes the Spec's `setters` list a contract rather
# than a hint: a widget wrapped with a value prop and no setter beside it is an
# incomplete declaration, which is a thing to fix rather than to discover by
# looking at the screen.
#
# The stub declares one, because no shipping widget in fyne.sngl is missing a
# setter -- which is the point. Testing it needs a widget written wrong on
# purpose.

! sngl generate --lang go --platform fyne --out out .
stderr 'has no setter for "text"'
stderr 'reaches the screen not at all'

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import fyne "sngl:platform/fyne"

// A Fyne widget wrapped without the setter its value prop needs.
component broken(value string) ui.node {
    fyne.Widget(
        spec=fyne.Spec{
            new = fyne.Native{path="fyne.io/fyne/v2/widget", name="NewLabel"},
            args = [fyne.Arg{raw=`""`}],
            goType = fyne.Native{path="fyne.io/fyne/v2/widget", name="*Label"},
            setters = [],
        },
        text=value,
    ) {}
}

ui.window #w(title="t") {
    var greeting = "hello"

    broken(value=greeting)

    ui.button(text="x", @click {
        greeting = "bye"
    })
}
